tools.name: get_docs
tools.description: Fetch Ptally documentation by topic. Call BEFORE building or editing a config to load the rules and reference material you need. Topics: "rules" = agent rules, constraints, expression syntax, quality gates, and debugging guidance (start here); "readme" = full engine reference with step types, query

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Fetch the full JSON schema for Ptally project config files. Use to check exact field requirements, allowed step types, and property constraints.

tools.name: validate_project
tools.description: Server-side schema validation of a project config. Returns { valid: true/false, errors: [...] } with the JSON path, keyword, and message for each issue. Prefer local validation against get_schema during authoring; use this as a ground-truth check, including on an amended model before handing it back

tools.name: get_starter
tools.description: Fetch a worked-example Ptally project for a common line of business. Each example is a small, fully valid project with realistic collection tables, calculations, exclusions and refers, plus an embedded tests[] suite for reference. Use as a template — copy and adapt rather than authoring from scratch

tools.name: get_projects
tools.description: List every project stored on this self-host instance. Returns `{ count, projects: [{ project_reference, name, description }] }`. Descriptions are truncated to 100 characters so the response stays compact — call get_project for the full record. Archived projects are excluded.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Fetch a project by `project_reference` from the self-host store. Optional `version_reference` pins to a specific version of that project (a version from another project is a tool error); otherwise the latest live (published or approved) version is used, or the latest non-archived version of any stat

tools.name: run_quote
tools.description: Dry-run a quote against a stored project. Takes `project_reference`, an optional `version_reference` (defaults to the latest live version; there is no fallback to drafts, so pass `version_reference` to price one — it must belong to the project and not be archived, else a tool error), and an `input`

tools.name: run_version_tests
tools.description: Price every test in a version's tests[] against that version's stored model and compare each with its expected output. Takes `version_reference` (any status but archived — a draft after patch_version, or a live version for a baseline). Runs against the stored model, so a patch saved a moment ago is

tools.name: patch_version
tools.description:
Change a DRAFT version's stored model with an RFC 6902 JSON Patch, merged on the server. Use it for targeted edits; any change to a clipped collection (__context.patchable: false) goes through download and upload instead (see next_steps in get_project).

BEFORE CALLING
1. The version must be a draft

tools.name: get_health
tools.description: Diagnostic snapshot of the deployed MCP server plus a live probe of its store (sqlite or Postgres). Returns server name and version, protocol version, root, boot time, advertised tool names and count, a hash of the tool surface, and `store` — `{ ok, latency_ms, counts: { projects, quotes } }` from c

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "patch_version" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "patch_version" is 3762 chars, far longer than this server's median (455). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_project · Private data: get_schema, validate_project, get_projects, get_project, run_version_tests · Public sink: patch_version · Destructive: get_project, run_quote, run_version_tests, patch_version.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_project · Private data: get_schema, validate_project, get_projects, get_project, run_version_tests · Public sink: patch_version · Destructive: get_project, run_quote, run_version_tests, patch_version

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
